$comment: Component CSS rules that dim a disabled control with `opacity < 1`. The guard is about TEXT: dimming a label composites it down to ~2:1 against its surface, which reads as 'hard to read' rather than 'unavailable'. Three sites were found this way (tabs, segmented, filter-chip) and all three were fixed to express disabled with a muted token instead. An entry here is only legitimate when the dimmed thing is a GLYPH rather than text, and it must say why. This list only shrinks.

entries.platform/ui/components/icon-button/iconB: dims the GLYPH of an icon-only control (no text to composite); a disabled control is exempt from the non-text contrast floor, which applies to controls a reader can operate. Boundary: this covers only the pure-icon disabled state — the `loading` state is NOT covered, its arc must stay >= 3:1 (it has its own colour rule), so an exemption must never be read as permission to dim a waiting indicator
